# Commits whose PHI-pattern match in git history is DEMONSTRABLY SYNTHETIC.
#
# The history scan uses `git log -S`, which matches a commit when the count of a
# term CHANGES -- so it flags the commit that REMOVED a string as well as the one
# that added it. That is correct behaviour for a leak scanner (the blob is still
# in history either way) but it means a fabricated test fixture is indistinguishable
# from real PHI without an explicit judgement.
#
# EVERY ENTRY MUST NAME THE STRING AND WHY IT IS NOT PHI. This file is a
# permanent hole in a CRITICAL gate, so it stays as small as possible. If you
# cannot state plainly why the content is fabricated, the answer is to purge the
# history, not to add a line here.
#
# 5d22d50  added   tests/testthat/test-nightly-ci-contract.R
# 24d772c  removed same
#   String: printf "PatientName,MRN\nJane Roe,00123\n" > leak.csv
#   A probe planted into a mktemp throwaway git repository to prove the scanner
#   actually fires -- "a scanner that has never fired is indistinguishable from
#   one that cannot". The name is a placeholder, the MRN is 00123, and the file
#   never existed outside the fixture. 24d772c replaced the literal with a
#   runtime-assembled string precisely so the scanner would stop matching it.
5d22d50
24d772c
#
# 1140962  added   tests/testthat/test-nightly-ci-contract.R (scan-phi-dua.sh's
#                   own creation commit)
# 47b7e15  removed same
#   String: printf "PatientName,MRN\nJane Roe,00123\n" > leak.csv
#   The FIRST occurrence of the identical 5d22d50/24d772c pair above, from when
#   the leak guard and its self-test were originally authored: 1140962 created
#   scan-phi-dua.sh (whose own PHI_COLS pattern list names "PatientName" as a
#   column NAME to search for, not a value) together with a probe using the
#   same literal fixture string; 47b7e15 is the very next day's fix, replacing
#   the literal with a runtime-assembled string for the same reason 24d772c
#   documents. Verified via git show: both diffs are byte-identical to the
#   5d22d50/24d772c pair's content, just an earlier point in the file's
#   history before it was touched again.
1140962
47b7e15
